name: Expository Essay
purpose: Explains or informs on a topic using facts and examples while staying neutral — the writer's opinion isn't the point.

components.note: States a topic or fact, not an opinion — the line that distinguishes this from persuasive writing.
Facts, examples, or data — not the writer's opinion.
Synthesizes what the evidence adds up to, rather than repeating the thesis.

organizational_patterns.name: Chronological
organizational_patterns.description: Orders the explanation by time or sequence.

organizational_patterns.name: Classification
organizational_patterns.description: Sorts the topic into categories and explains each in turn.

organizational_patterns.name: Compare/Contrast
organizational_patterns.description: See the compare-contrast essay type — a named subtype of expository.

organizational_patterns.name: Cause and Effect
organizational_patterns.description: See the cause-effect essay type — a named subtype of expository.

organizational_patterns.name: Process
organizational_patterns.description: See the process essay type — a named subtype of expository.

pitfalls: The thesis smuggles in an opinion, drifting into persuasive writing without arguing for the position.
Body paragraphs restate the thesis instead of adding new evidence.
Evidence presented with no topic sentence, so the reader can't tell what point it's proving.
